svg.text: 12 V power: battery, fuses, key, dash rail, bucks
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'power'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: P01: BAT12.pos -> FB.IN - 60 A main fuse at the battery. Was 6 mm² in wiring.md, which the table only rates to 40 A
P02: FB.F12 -> KEY.BAT
P03: KEY.IGN -> RAIL.BUS
P04: FB.F8 -> RELAYS.COM8
P05: RELAYS.NO8 -> RAIL.BUS - Power hold, in parallel with the key
P06: RAIL.BUS -> TVS.K
P07: RAIL.BUS -> PI_BUCK.VIN
P08: RAIL.BUS -> PICO_BUCK.VIN - 2 A inline fuse
P09: PI_BUCK.VOUT -> PI5.5V - Short and thick, under 30 cm. Set usb_max_current_enable=1
P10: PICO_BUCK.VOUT -> PICO.VSYS
P11: PICO_BUCK.VOUT -> RELAYS.JDVCC - Relay coils, about 0.6 A for 8
P12: PICO_BUCK.VOUT -> RELAYS2.JDVCC
P13: RAIL.BUS -> SCREEN_PSU.VIN - Fuse size depends on the screen's draw
P14: SCREEN_PSU.VOUT -> SCREEN.DC_IN
P15: FB.F7 -> RELAYS.COM7 - Accessory 12 V, on with ignition
P20: RELAYS.NO7 -> GLOVE_USB.VIN - 3 A inline fuse. Charges the RC phone with the key on; the control box may hold it on for a while after key-off (TBC)
P16: BAT12.pos -> AMP.B+ - Own fuse at the battery. 4 x 50 W can pull 20-30 A
P17: RAIL.BUS -> AMP.REM - Remote turn-on, goes off with the rail
P18: DCDC.out_pos -> BAT12.pos - DC-DC charge lead. Size and fuse depend on its rating
P19: BAT12.pos -> EPS_ECU.B+ - Own 60 A fuse and cable straight to the battery (Toyota fuses the Prius EPS at 60 A)
BAT12: 12 V aux battery - Kept after the conversion. Charged by the DC-DC

FB: Blade fuse block - 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. A 20-way leaves 8 spares
g.text: F7 extras - interior bar + relay 7 acc…

g.title: AMP: 12 V marine amp
DCDC: DC-DC converter 72 V to 12 V - Charges the 12 V battery. Rating TBC; it decides how long winch + steering can run
EPS_ECU: Toyota Aqua EPS ECU (89650-52B51) - Wrecker column, bench test with the Prius CAN frames first. ECU plug pinout TBC

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
KEY: Teryx key switch
RAIL: Dash 12 V rail - Key OR relay 8 (power hold). Stays up after key-off until the Pico lets go

GLOVE_USB: Glove box USB-C charger (RC phone) - 12 V to USB-C PD socket for the phone that lives in the glove box (docs/rc-beach-launch.md 4b). Fed from the accessory relay so it's off with the key off
TVS: 1.5KE18A TVS diode - Clamps spikes on the dash rail
PI_BUCK: Pololu D36V50F5 5 V 5.5 A - Pi 5 power. About 16 W of its 27 W with the AI HAT+ 2 fitted
PICO_BUCK: Mini560 5 V buck (control box)
SCREEN_PSU: Screen 12 V supply - Depends on the screen's power brick. If it is 12 V, a 12 V stabiliser
PI5: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB - The 40-pin header and the PCIe port are kept for the AI HAT+ 2. CAN module wires go to header pins that come up through the HAT
PICO: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
RELAYS2: 16-ch relay board, channels 9-16 (2 used, 6 spare) - Same board as RELAYS. Relay 9 steering enable, relay 10 drive lock (uses the NC contact)
SCREEN: 10.1 in touch screen - 1280x800, HDMI + USB touch, 3.5 mm audio in
